> **Updated October 4, 2026.** I re-checked every course on NVIDIA's own pages. A lot changed since this guide first went up in May: *Getting Started with Deep Learning*, *Generative AI Explained* and the RAPIDS data science course have been retired, and *Building RAG Agents with LLMs* and *Fundamentals of Accelerated Computing with CUDA Python* are now **$90**. This version replaces the old list.

**Short answer: NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute (DLI) is partly free.** Right now there are **10 free self-paced courses**, mostly on agentic AI, Omniverse, OpenUSD and robotics. The core deep learning, RAG and CUDA courses cost **$30–$90**, and NVIDIA certification exams start at **$125**. The best free way to learn deep learning from NVIDIA today is the open-source **Fundamentals of Deep Learning** course on GitHub, but it gives no certificate.

---

## What NVIDIA DLI offers and what it costs

| Format | Price | Certificate | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free self-paced courses | Free | Not stated on the free course pages | [Free courses list](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/training/self-paced-courses/#free-courses) |
| Paid self-paced courses | $30 (2–4 h) or $90 (8 h) | Yes, on courses with an assessment | [Self-paced catalog](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/training/self-paced-courses/) |
| Open-source courses | Free, no sign-up | No | [Open source courses](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/training/open-source/) |
| Instructor-led workshops | From $500 per seat | Yes | [Find training](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/training/find-training/) |
| Certification exams | $125 (Associate), $200–$500 (Professional) | Digital badge, valid 2 years | [Certification](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/learn/certification/) |

Self-paced courses run in the browser on a **GPU-accelerated cloud workstation**, so you don't need your own NVIDIA GPU. Purchases (courses and exam vouchers) can't be refunded, so check the outline before you pay.

---

## The 10 free NVIDIA DLI courses right now

Checked on NVIDIA's self-paced course page on October 4, 2026:

| Course | Topic | Length |
|---|---|---|
| [Agentic AI Explained](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-FX-39+V1) | What AI agents are, no coding | 1 h |
| [Securing Agents with NemoClaw and OpenShell](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-FX-43+V1) | Agent security, hands-on | 4 h |
| [A Beginner's Guide to Autonomous Robots](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-OV-35+V1) | Robotics basics | 1 h |
| [Generating High-Quality Motion Data for Robotics With MobilityGen](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-OV-37+V1) | Robot training data | 1.5 h |
| [Software-in-the-Loop Testing for Robots With OpenUSD, Isaac Sim, and ROS](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-OV-39+V1) | Robot simulation testing | 2 h |
| [An Introduction to Developing With NVIDIA Omniverse](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-OV-11+V1) | Omniverse basics | 2 h |
| [Fundamentals of Working With OpenUSD](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-OV-15+V1) | 3D scene format | 2 h |
| [Creating an Omniverse Extension With Python](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-OV-16+V1) | Omniverse + Python | 2 h |
| [Extend Omniverse Kit Applications for Building Digital Twins](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-OV-13+V1) | Digital twins | 2 h |
| [Building AI-Powered Material Generation for Omniverse With DGX Cloud](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-OV-53+V1) | Generative materials | 2 h |

**My picks:** start with **Agentic AI Explained** (one hour, works for non-engineers and for briefing a team), then **Securing Agents with NemoClaw and OpenShell** if you build agents. Take the robotics and Omniverse courses only if that is your field; that's where most of the free catalog sits.

> 💡 The free list changes often. Courses marked "This course will soon be retired" stop taking enrollments on a fixed date, so enroll first and study later.

---

## The free NVIDIA deep learning course most guides miss

People searching for an "NVIDIA deep learning course" usually land on *Getting Started with Deep Learning*. That course is now $90 and being retired. The free replacement is **Fundamentals of Deep Learning**, released as an [NVIDIA open-source course](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/training/open-source/):

- Code, notebooks and lab guide are on [GitHub (NVDLI/fundamentals-of-deep-learning)](https://github.com/NVDLI/fundamentals-of-deep-learning) under Apache 2.0 / CC BY 4.0
- **No registration** needed. NVIDIA says it is the same quality as its paid courses
- You run it yourself: on your own NVIDIA GPU, or on a cloud GPU you pay for
- **No certificate**: NVIDIA says it does not issue certificates for open-source courses

If you want a solid deep learning foundation and don't need a certificate, this is the best free option NVIDIA has today.

---

## Do free NVIDIA courses come with a certificate?

**Mostly no.** NVIDIA issues certificates "in select courses", meaning courses with an assessment. None of the free course pages I checked mention a certificate, and open-source courses don't give one.

If the certificate is the goal, the realistic options are:

1. **A $90 course with an assessment.** [Building RAG Agents with LLMs](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-FX-15+V1) and [Fundamentals of Accelerated Computing with CUDA Python](https://learn.nvidia.com/courses/course-detail?course_id=course-v1:DLI+S-AC-10+V1) are both 8 hours, include a cloud GPU, and award a certificate when you pass the assessment.
2. **A certification exam** (next section), which is a proctored credential rather than a course certificate.

---

## Is NVIDIA certification free?

No. All exams are paid, taken online with a remote proctor through Certiverse, and **valid for two years**:

| Level | Examples | Price | Length |
|---|---|---|---|
| Associate | Generative AI LLMs (NCA-GENL), Generative AI Multimodal (NCA-GENM), AI Infrastructure and Operations (NCA-AIIO) | $125 | 1 h, 50–60 questions |
| Professional | Generative AI LLMs (NCP-GENL) and others | $200–$500 | 2 h |

For a first NVIDIA credential, **NCA-GENL** ($125) is the common entry point. Study with the free open-source deep learning course plus the free agentic AI course before you buy the exam.

---

## Ways to get paid DLI courses for free

- **University educators**: the [DLI Teaching Kit Program](https://developer.nvidia.com/teaching-kits) gives approved members codes for free self-paced courses for themselves and their students, "a value of up to $90 per course, per student".
- **Students**: ask your instructor or department whether they are in the Teaching Kit or [University Ambassador](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/training/educator-programs/) program. That is the official route.

> Correction: the earlier version of this guide said a university email could unlock paid labs. I found no such mechanism on NVIDIA's pages, so I removed it.

---

## Free official CUDA resources

The DLI CUDA Python course is now $90, so it is no longer a free entry point. These official resources are free:

- [An Even Easier Introduction to CUDA](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/even-easier-introduction-cuda/): NVIDIA's classic beginner tutorial (updated 2025)
- [CUDA C++ Programming Guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/): the reference
- [CUDA Python documentation](https://nvidia.github.io/cuda-python/): if you prefer Python

Pay the $90 for the DLI course only if you want the guided labs, a cloud GPU and the certificate.

---

## A beginner path that costs $0

1. **Agentic AI Explained**: 1 hour, the big picture
2. **Fundamentals of Deep Learning** (open source): neural network basics, hands-on
3. **An Even Easier Introduction to CUDA**: how GPU acceleration actually works
4. **Securing Agents with NemoClaw and OpenShell**: build and secure an agent

Spend money after that, and only on what you need: $90 for a certificate course, or $125 for NCA-GENL.

---

## FAQ

### Is NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute free?

Partly. As of October 2026 there are 10 free self-paced DLI courses, mostly on agentic AI, Omniverse, OpenUSD and robotics. Most deep learning, RAG and CUDA courses cost $30 or $90, instructor-led workshops start at $500, and certification exams cost $125 or more.

### Do NVIDIA free courses give a certificate?

Usually not. NVIDIA gives certificates in select courses that have an assessment, and those are mostly the paid $90 courses. Open-source courses such as Fundamentals of Deep Learning give no certificate.

### Is there a free NVIDIA deep learning course?

Yes: Fundamentals of Deep Learning is free as an NVIDIA open-source course on GitHub (NVDLI/fundamentals-of-deep-learning). It needs no registration, but you supply the GPU and there is no certificate. The older Getting Started with Deep Learning course is now $90 and being retired.

### How much do NVIDIA DLI courses cost?

Paid self-paced courses cost $30 (2–4 hours) or $90 (8 hours). Public instructor-led workshops start at $500 per seat. Purchases are not refundable.

### Is NVIDIA certification free?

No. Associate exams cost $125 and Professional exams cost $200 to $500. All are proctored online through Certiverse and valid for two years.

### Where can I learn CUDA for free?

Use NVIDIA's free tutorial "An Even Easier Introduction to CUDA", the CUDA C++ Programming Guide, and the CUDA Python documentation. The DLI course Fundamentals of Accelerated Computing with CUDA Python now costs $90.

### Do I need my own GPU for NVIDIA DLI courses?

Not for self-paced DLI courses: they run on a GPU-accelerated cloud workstation in your browser. Open-source courses are different, because you run them on your own NVIDIA GPU or on a cloud GPU you pay for.

---

## The One-Sentence Summary

> **NVIDIA DLI is no longer the free deep learning school it used to be: the free catalog is now mostly agentic AI, Omniverse and robotics, and the classic deep learning, RAG and CUDA courses cost $90. The best free deep learning material from NVIDIA has moved to its open-source courses on GitHub.**
